examples: I show my passport at the airport.
I put the passport in my bag.
nuance: 여권 is the official booklet that proves who you are when you travel to another country.
mistakes: Confusing 여권 (passport) with 비자, the entry permit stamp.

examples: I go city sightseeing on weekends.
This city is famous for sightseeing.
nuance: 관광 means traveling around to enjoy famous places and scenery, usually as a relaxed visitor.
mistakes: Using 관광 for a business trip; that is 출장 instead.

examples: There are very many tourists here.
nuance: 관광객 is a person who visits a place for sightseeing and fun, not someone who lives there.
mistakes: Saying 관광 for the person; the visitor is the 관광객.

examples: I bought a souvenir on the trip.
I gave a souvenir to my friend.
nuance: 기념품 is a small item you buy on a trip to remember the place or give to people back home.
mistakes: Using 선물 for every trip item; a trip keepsake is 기념품.

examples: I pack luggage before the trip.
I left my luggage at the hotel.
nuance: 짐 means the bags and things you carry when you travel or move, often heavy to lift.
mistakes: Using 짐 only for boxes; it also covers travel bags.

examples: I pull my suitcase at the airport.
I put clothes in the big suitcase.
nuance: 캐리어 is a hard rolling suitcase with wheels and a handle that you pull along when you travel.
mistakes: Calling a soft 가방 a 캐리어; this one rolls on wheels.

examples: I wear a backpack when hiking.
I put water and bread in the backpack.
We went on a backpacking trip.
nuance: 배낭 is a large bag you carry on your back, handy for hiking or simple budget travel.
mistakes: Saying 배낭을 들어요; you wear it, so use 배낭을 메요.

examples: I arrived at the lodging at night.
nuance: 숙소 is a general word for any place you stay overnight on a trip, like a hotel or guesthouse.
mistakes: Using 집 for a travel stay; the place you sleep is 숙소.

examples: The travel itinerary is very busy.
We made the plan in advance.
nuance: 일정 is the planned schedule of where you go and what you do each day during a trip.
mistakes: Confusing 일정 (schedule) with 시간, which is just clock time.

examples: The train departure is a bit late.
Our departure is at seven a.m.
nuance: 출발 means leaving to begin a trip, the moment a person or vehicle starts moving away.
mistakes: Mixing up 출발 (departure) with 도착, which means arrival.

examples: The plane arrival is an hour late.
I tell my friend the arrival time.
Our arrival is at eight p.m.
nuance: 도착 means reaching the place you traveled to, the moment a person or vehicle gets there.
mistakes: Mixing up 도착 (arrival) with 출발, which means departure.

examples: I bought a museum admission ticket.
I show the ticket to the staff.
nuance: 입장권 is the ticket that lets you enter a place like a museum, park, or show.
mistakes: Using 표 for entry; an entrance ticket is the 입장권.
